column1: Okay, let's get started. So I've put up the homework that's due on Wednesday, where we're going to finish up this first chapter on group theory, and then we're going to take a little time away from group theory and enter into the theory of vector spaces over general fields.
column2: 好的，我们开始上课。我已经布置了周三交的作业，周三我们将结束群论的第一章，然后我们会暂时离开群论，进入一般域上的向量空间理论。

column1: So you probably studied vector spaces over the real and complex numbers; we're going to study them a little bit more abstractly and do linear algebra in its full level of generality,
column2: 大家可能学过实数域和复数域上的向量空间；我们将更抽象地研究它们，在完全一般性的层面上讨论线性代数，

column1: and then we're going to return to do more on groups. So let me remember where Peter left you last time: we have this wonderful group, which is the integers under addition.
column2: 然后再回到群论深入探讨。让我回忆一下彼得上次讲到了哪里：我们有这样一个极佳的群，即整数在加法下构成的群。

column1: That's our basic group, and we identified all the subgroups, which have the form n times the integers where n is some integer greater than or equal to zero — so the multiples of some fixed integer, that's what we showed way back when we did the structure of this group.
column2: 这是我们的基本群，我们之前找出了它的所有子群，它们都具有 n 倍整数的形式（nZ），其中 n 是某个大于或等于零的整数——即某个固定整数的倍数，这是我们很久前研究该群结构时证明的。

column1: Remember, we used the Euclidean algorithm to prove that.
column2: 记得吧，我们用辗转相除法（欧几里得算法）证明了这一点。

column1: And last time, Peter associated to every subgroup — so this is our subgroup H, this is our group G, each H in G — a new group which he denoted Z mod nZ. So that's notation that's due to Gauss.
column2: 上次彼得把每个子群——这是我们的子群 H，这是我们的群 G，G 中的每个 H——都关联到一个新群，他记作 Z/nZ（Z mod nZ）。这个记号出自高斯。

column1: So this would be called Z mod n.
column2: 所以这读作 Z mod n。

column1: This notation and this group were defined on the first sentence of Gauss's great book, the Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, published in 1801,
column2: 这个记号和这个群是在高斯的名著《算术研究》（DisquisitionesArithmeticae）第一句中定义的，

column1: where this — the notation mod n comes from the Latin word modulus. The Disquisitiones is written in Latin.
column2: 该书出版于 1801 年。这里的记号 mod n 源自拉丁语单词 modulus。《算术研究》是用拉丁文写的。

column1: If I can get the first two pages for you from Houghton Library, I'll print them out and distribute them; they're a précis of mathematical writing.
column2: 要是我能从霍顿图书馆（Houghton Library）帮你们搞到前两页，我会印出来发给大家；那是数学写作的精要典范。

column1: And this new group Z mod nZ consists of the classes of integers where you only keep track of their remainder after division by n.
column2: 而这个新群 Z/nZ 由整数的等价类构成，其中你只追踪它们被 n 除后的余数。

column1: So we have elements a-bar in Z mod nZ, and a-bar depends on the remainder of the integer a after division by n.
column2: 所以我们在 Z/nZ 中有元素 a-bar，且 a-bar 取决于整数 a 除以 n 的余数。

column1: So in particular, if a and b are integers, we have a-bar equal to b-bar, or as Gauss would write it, a congruent to b mod n — that's Gauss's notation — we'd say a-bar is equal to b-bar in the group Z mod nZ if and only if n divides a minus b.
column2: 特别地，如果 a 和 b 是整数，在群 Z/nZ 中 a-bar 等于 b-bar，或者按高斯的写法，a ≡ b (mod n)——那是高斯的记号——我们在群 Z/nZ 中说 a-bar 等于 b-bar 当且仅当n 整除 a − b。

column1: And so in particular, this new group, which only depends on the remainder, has only n elements in it.
column2: 所以特别地，这个只取决于余数的新群只包含 n 个元素。

column1: So this new group, you could say, consists of the elements 0-bar, 1-bar, 2-bar, up to n minus 1-bar, because those are the only things that are possible remainders.
column2: 因此你可以说，这个新群由元素 0-bar、1-bar、2-bar 一直到 (n−1)-bar 组成，因为只有这些是可能的余数。

column1: That's the group Z mod nZ. And the addition law is by adding two things in the integers and then calculating the remainder after division by n.
column2: 这就是群 Z/nZ。它的加法法则是在整数中将两数相加，然后计算除以 n后的余数。

column1: So a-bar plus b-bar in Z mod nZ is equal to (a plus b)-bar, namely add them in the integers — this is in Z — and then take the remainder after reducing mod n.
column2: 所以 Z/nZ 中的 a-bar + b-bar 等于 (a+b)-bar，即在整数中相加——这属于 Z——然后取模 n 约化后的余数。

column1: And this gives the structure of a group on this set of n elements, and in fact it's a cyclic group of order n generated by the class 1-bar, because if you take 1-bar and you add it to itself you get 2-bar, and then if you add 1-bar you get 3-bar,
column2: 这就在这 n 个元素的集合上赋予了群结构，事实上它是一个 n 阶循环群，由等价类 1-bar 生成；因为如果你取 1-bar 加上自身，就得到 2-bar，再加上 1-bar 就得到 3-bar，

column1: and yet another one you get 4-bar, and you get up to n minus 1-bar, and then you add one to that, you get back to the identity element. So this gives another description of a cyclic group of order n. Remember we claimed that there was one for each value n.
column2: 再加一个得到 4-bar，一直加到 (n−1)-bar，然后再加 1-bar，就回到了单位元。这就给出了 n 阶循环群的另一种描述。记得我们曾断言对每个 n 值都存在这样的群。

column1: This is the notation I'll use for a cyclic group of order n.
column2: 这就是我用来表示 n 阶循环群的记号。

column1: It has the advantage that it not only is a cyclic group, but it has a natural generator 1-bar, just like the integers are a cyclic group with a natural generator 1.
column2: 它的优势在于，它不仅是一个循环群，而且具有自然的生成元 1-bar，正如整数是具有自然生成元 1 的循环群一样。

column1: This is an infinite cyclic group; this is a finite cyclic group of every order n.
column2: 这是无限循环群，而这是每个阶数 n 的有限循环群。

column1: Moreover, we have a natural group homomorphism f from Z to Z mod nZ which takes the class of a to the class of a-bar, i.e., a mod n, the remainder of a after division by n.
column2: 此外，我们有一个自然的群同态 f: Z → Z/nZ，它把a 的类映为 a-bar 的类，即 a mod n，即 a 除以 n 的余数。

column1: And this is a group homomorphism, a homomorphism which is onto, which is surjective, because every class in this group is the remainder of something — surjective with kernel nZ, namely the things that go to 0-bar are exactly the things divisible by n. So there's our subgroup.
column2: 这是一个群同态，一个满射同态，因为这个群里的每个类都是某个数的余数——是核为 nZ 的满同态，即映到 0-bar 的元素恰好是能被 n 整除的数。这就是我们的子群。

column1: So to recapitulate what Peter did last time — and this is a great construction of Gauss's, which is the first example of this in the literature in 1801, before Galois had invented the general notion of a group — associated to each subgroup of the integers under addition, we construct a new group, which is called the quotient group.
column2: 所以总结一下彼得上次所讲的内容——这是高斯的伟大构想，也是 1801 年文献中该概念的首个范例，比伽罗瓦提出抽象群的一般概念还要早——对应于加法整数群的每个子群，我们构造了一个新群，称为商群。

column1: We're going to do that more generally this time: the quotient group, such that there is a surjective homomorphism from the group to the quotient group with kernel the subgroup.
column2: 今天我们要更一般地讨论商群：从原群到商群存在一个满同态，且以该子群为核。

column1: Okay. Now this is a much richer case than the average group, and the reason it's a richer case — and Peter went into this a little bit last time, and we'll return to it — is that the integers have a much richer structure than just addition, right? The integers also have the product structure, multiplication.
column2: 好的。这比一般的群情形要丰富得多，之所以更丰富——彼得上节课也稍微涉及过，我们还会再讲——是因为整数拥有远比单纯加法更丰富的结构，对吧？整数还具有乘积结构，即乘法。

column1: Namely, the integers not only form a group under addition, they form a ring. So they also have the operation times.
column2: 具体而言，整数不仅在加法下构成群，还构成一个环。所以它们还有乘法运算。

column1: And when you have both in a group addition and a multiplication structure and they're suitably compatible, that's what we call a ring. And we're going to get to that, I promise you this term.
column2: 当你在一个群中同时拥有加法和乘法结构，并且它们适当相容时，我们就称之为环。我保证本学期我们会讲到环。

column1: And in fact, this quotient group also has the structure of a ring: you can multiply remainders and it's still compatible.
column2: 事实上，这个商群也具有环的结构：你可以把余数相乘，且它依然相容。

column1: Namely, you can define a-bar times b-bar by taking a times b in the integers and then taking its remainder, and that's a well-defined multiplication.
column2: 即你可以通过在整数中计算 a 乘 b 并取其余数来定义 a-bar × b-bar，且该乘法是良定义的。

column1: So this is not just a finite cyclic group of order n, but it also allows you to multiply elements in it. That's a remarkable property.
column2: 因此这不仅是一个n 阶有限循环群，而且还允许你将其中的元素相乘。这是个非凡的性质。

column1: And most of the Disquisitiones, in fact one might say all of the Disquisitiones, is concerned with the properties of those finite rings: quadratic reciprocity theorem, quartic reciprocity — all these great results that Gauss discovered are about the properties of this finite ring.
column2: 《算术研究》的大部分内容，事实上可以说是《算术研究》的全部内容，都在关注这些有限环的性质：二次互反律、四次互反律——高斯发现的所有这些伟大成果，都与这个有限环的性质有关。

column1: And Peter discovered — well, introduced you last time to another thing: you see, if you have a ring — and I'm just going to say this very briefly, it's not necessary right now: so you have both, it's a group under plus with an origin, and then there's a times operation with an identity element 1, but not necessarily inverses.
column2: 彼得上次还向大家介绍了另一件事：你看，如果你有一个环——我只简要提一下，现在不是必须掌握的：你兼有两者，它在加法下是带零元的群，然后还有一个带单位元 1 的乘法运算，但不一定有乘法逆元。

column1: For example, 0 has no inverse; you can't multiply anything by 0 and get to 1.
column2: 例如 0 没有逆元；任何数乘以 0 都不可能得到 1。

column1: Nonetheless, you get a subset of the ring called R-star, which is sometimes called the units of the ring, which is the set of elements a in R such that there exists a b such that ab is equal to 1. So they're the elements which have multiplicative inverses; everything has an additive inverse.
column2: 尽管如此，你还是能得到环的一个子集，记作 R*（R-star），有时称为环的单位群（可逆元群），即 R 中满足如下条件的元素 a 的集合：存在 b 使得 ab = 1。所以它们是具有乘法逆元的元素；每个元素都有加法逆元。

column1: Now that can be a rather small — and this is another group.
column2: 这个集合可能相当小——而这是另一个群。

column1: So a ring is a group under addition, and you get a second group from a ring, which is the unit group, which is a group under multiplication. And it can be a rather small group.
column2: 所以环在加法下是一个群，并且你从环中还能得到第二个群，即单位群，它是乘法下的群。它可能是一个相当小的群。

column1: For example, this is the most famous ring of them all, the integers — all rings are modeled on the integers — if you ask yourself, what is the multiplicative group associated to the integers, namely which integers have multiplicative inverses?
column2: 例如，对于最著名的环——整数环（所有环都以整数为模型）——如果你问自己：与整数相关联的乘法群是什么？即哪些整数具有乘法逆元？

column1: The answer is very simple: just +1 and -1. There is no multiplicative inverse for 2 because 1/2 is not an integer.
column2: 答案非常简单：只有 +1 和 -1。2 没有乘法逆元，因为 1/2 不是整数。

column1: So for this ring, we would find that the multiplicative group here is just the group on two elements, plus or minus one. It's a kind of a stupid group, but there it is.
column2: 所以对于这个环，我们会发现这里的乘法群只是一个二元群 {±1}。这是个有点微不足道的群，但它确实存在。

column1: On the other hand, as Peter pointed out, these finite rings have very interesting multiplicative groups, very interesting, and we're going to get into that later when we do the ring theory.
column2: 另一方面，正如彼得所指出的，这些有限环具有非常有趣的乘法群，非常有趣，稍后我们讲环论时会深入讨论。

column1: And Gauss was the first person to work out the structure of the multiplicative group of units in those rings.
column2: 高斯是第一个弄清这些环中可逆元乘法群结构的人。

column1: But right now, for the point of view of this lecture, it's only important that we inherit the additive group structure and that we have this additive group homomorphism.
column2: 但眼下，就本讲的视角而言，重要的是我们继承了加法群结构，并且拥有这个加法群同态。

column1: Before I go any further, are there questions on this construction? Because it's very basic; it's the model for what we're going to follow when we do a quotient group in general.
column2: 在继续之前，关于这个构造有什么问题吗？因为这是非常基础的，它是我们接下来讨论一般商群时的范本。

column1: Okay, so let me be a little bit more general than this. Now this is a particularly simple group.
column2: 好的，那么让我讨论比这更一般的情形。这是一个特别简单的群。

column1: As I said to you, this is an abelian group, so we have to pay attention and see what properties are we really using of these subgroups when we construct this quotient group. Can we do it for any subgroup, or is there some peculiar property of the subgroup that we need?
column2: 正如我刚才所说，这是一个交换群（阿贝尔群），所以我们必须注意，看看在构造这个商群时我们究竟利用了这些子群的什么性质。我们对任何子群都能构造商群吗，还是需要子群具备某种特殊性质？

column1: So let me start off in a simple situation where the subgroup is defined by a group homomorphism. By the way, these classes in Z mod nZ are just the cosets of this subgroup — represent the cosets of nZ, the distinct cosets.
column2: 所以让我先从一种简单情形开始：子群由一个群同态所定义。顺便说一下，Z/nZ 中的这些等价类正好就是这个子群的陪集——代表了 nZ 的陪集，即各个不相交的陪集。

column1: So the quotient group as a set is the set of cosets of the subgroup, and yet we're able to give a multiplication on it. So that's going to be our question: when can we put a group structure on the set of all cosets?
column2: 所以商群作为一个集合，就是该子群的陪集集合，但我们却能给它定义乘法。这就是我们所要探讨的问题：何时能给所有陪集的集合赋予群结构？

column1: H, for a subgroup H in G, we always get a — we have a subgroup, we get a set: its set of cosets. And we've seen that that gives a partition of the group.
column2: 对于 G 中的子群 H，我们总能得到一个——有了子群，就得到一个集合：它的陪集集合。我们已经看到它给出了原群的一个划分。

column1: Here's our group, here's H, here's aH, here's bH; so we get a nice partition of the group into cosets.
column2: 这是我们的群，这是 H，这是 aH，这是 bH；所以我们得到了群的一个很好的陪集划分。

column1: So the set of cosets is a nice set. When can we get a group structure on it? So one case, Case 1: suppose H is equal to the kernel of a homomorphism f from G to G'. That's one way we get subgroups.
column2: 因此陪集集合是一个很好的集合。我们何时能在这个集合上定义群结构？第一种情形，情形 1：假设 H 是某个从 G 到 G' 的同态 f 的核。这是我们得到子群的一种方式。

column1: Then the set of cosets aH is in bijection with what? What do we — how do we get a coset out of a homomorphism?
column2: 那么陪集集合 aH 与什么成双射？我们怎么——怎么从同态中得到陪集？

column1: Remember that H was the kernel of it; what are the other cosets? The — yeah, the fibers! Exactly right.
column2: 记住，H 是它的核；其他陪集是什么？是——对，纤维！完全正确。

column1: Namely, we had a map here from G to G'; it needn't be a surjective map, but above each point in G', a-bar, we have the fiber, which is an entire coset of the kernel.
column2: 具体来说，我们这里有一个从 G 到 G' 的映射；它不必是满射，但在 G' 中的每个点 a-bar 上方，都有它的纤维，这是核的一个完整陪集。

column1: And we have another point here, b-bar, you've got its fiber: all the things mapping to b-bar, right? So the set of cosets are the fibers of the map.
column2: 并且我们在这里有另一个点 b-bar，有它的纤维：所有映射到 b-bar 的元素，对吧？所以陪集集合就是这个映射的纤维。

column1: So therefore, they can be identified bijectively with the points a-bar in the image, which is contained in G', correct?
column2: 因此，它们可以双射地等同于像集（包含在 G' 中）中的点 a-bar，对吧？

column1: Each coset corresponds bijectively to a point in the image, which is some little thing in here, image of f. And the image of a homomorphism is what, among other things?
column2: 每个陪集都双射对应于像集中的一个点，就是这里的某个子集 im f。而同态的像是什么？归根结底它是一个子群！

column1: It's a subgroup! The image of f is a subgroup; it's stable under multiplication in G' — a subgroup of G'. Therefore, since the set of cosets is in bijection with the set of the image, and we have a group structure on the image set, that gives us a group structure on the set of cosets, right?
column2: f 的像是一个子群；在 G' 的乘法下是封闭的——是 G' 的子群。因此，既然陪集集合与像集构成双射，且我们在像集上拥有群结构，这就赋予了我们陪集集合上的群结构，对吧？

column1: Good. So we transfer — sometimes mathematicians, if they wanted to be sophisticated, would say we transport the structure of the image onto the set of cosets.
column2: 很好。所以我们转移——有时数学家若想显得高深，会说我们把像集的结构转移（transport）到陪集集合上；如果你想显得更高深，可以用法语来说，

column1: Or if you want to be even more sophisticated, you say it in French, because that's a favorite expression of Bourbaki, that wrote up a lot of 20th-century mathematics: you'd say, par transport de structure,
column2: 因为那是布尔巴基（Bourbaki）最喜欢的表达，他们重构了 20 世纪的大量数学：你会说 par transport de structure（通过结构转移），

column1: or on en déduit une structure of the group, sur l'ensemble des cosets... Okay, coset is what in French? Cosette? Did I do that right? Not bad. You must learn French if you aspire to be a mathematician.
column2: 在陪集集合上诱导出群结构……法语里陪集怎么说？Cosette（珂赛特）？我说对了吗？还不错。立志成为数学家的话，必须学法语；要想把事情说得无比精确，就必须用法语说！

column1: If you want to say things precisely, they must be said in French! English is, of course, the worldwide language of mathematics and science nowadays, and has become even more so in the last 25 years, but there's certain types of mathematics you can only say in French!
column2: 当然，英语如今是全世界数学和科学的通用语言，在过去的 25 年里更是如此，但某类数学你只能用法语来表达！

column1: So we say, par transport de structure, we get a group structure on the set, and we'll call that set G mod H, of cosets.
column2: 所以我们说，par transport de structure，我们在该集合上得到了群结构，我们把这个陪集集合称为 G/H（G mod H）。

column1: And the group structure has the following form: when you multiply the coset aH by the coset bH, then I claim that the answer is — which coset is the product?
column2: 该群结构具有如下形式：当你把陪集 aH 与陪集 bH 相乘时，我断言结果是——哪一个陪集是这个乘积？

column1: It's just the coset of ab times H. Why?
column2: 正好就是 (ab)H 这个陪集。为什么？

column1: Because if I want to figure out how to multiply this coset by this coset, I have to figure out how to multiply a-bar by b-bar, right? That's the multiplication law; I'm going to use the multiplication law in G'.
column2: 因为如果我想弄清楚如何把这个陪集与这个陪集相乘，我就必须搞清如何把 a-bar 与 b-bar 相乘，对吧？那是乘法法则；我将使用G' 中的乘法法则。

column1: So what is a-bar times b-bar? Well, it's the bar of something, because it's in the image. What is it the bar of?
column2: 那么 a-bar 乘以 b-bar 是什么？它是某物的 bar，因为它落在像集里。它是谁的 bar 呢？

column1: Well, we figure this out by writing a-bar as f(a) and writing b-bar as f(b), and then using the fact that f is a homomorphism, and then this element is just what we would call (ab)-bar.
column2: 我们这样来计算：把 a-bar 写成 f(a)，把 b-bar 写成 f(b)，然后利用 f 是同态这一事实，于是这个元素就是我们所说的 (ab)-bar。

column1: So the product of the image element a-bar by the image element b-bar is the bar of ab, where this multiplication takes place in G.
column2: 因此像集元素 a-bar 与像集元素 b-bar 的乘积就是 (ab)-bar，其中这个乘法发生在 G 中。

column1: So that's what I mean: so when you want to multiply two cosets, you just take an element a in one of them, you take an element b in the other, you take the product of those elements, and you take its coset.
